title: Looping Through Dictionaries
learningObjectives: Explain looping through dictionaries and when it is useful.
Use the relevant Python operations with correct syntax.
Predict the result of common operations and edge cases.
Distinguish mutation, return values and error behavior.
Apply the concept to a small data-processing task.

understand.concept: A for loop over a dictionary visits its keys. Use items to unpack key-value pairs and values when only values are needed. A dictionary view reflects changes to its underlying mapping.
understand.whyItMatters: Looping Through Dictionaries is useful when a program needs to organize, inspect or transform related data reliably.
understand.analogy: A dictionary is like a labeled set of drawers: a key identifies the drawer that contains a value.
understand.analogyLimit: A dictionary key is not a physical drawer; keys must be hashable and lookup follows Python's mapping rules.

explain.narrative:
## Looping Through Dictionaries

A for loop over a dictionary visits its keys. Use items to unpack key-value pairs and values when only values are needed. A dictionary view reflects changes to its underlying mapping.

## Choosing an operation

Read the example code and check whether the operation mutates the object, returns a new value, or may raise an exception. Use membership tests and defaults where input may be missing.

## Practical reasoning

The five examples progress from basic use to a small real-world pattern. Compare each expected output with the code before changing it.

examples.expectedOutput: Direct iteration yields keys in insertion order.
items returns pairs suitable for unpacking in a loop.
The loop accumulates each value into total.
A dictionary comprehension retains pairs that satisfy the condition.
